The function converts an input value of the DINT data type to a BOOL, BYTE, WORD, DWORD, INT, UINT UDINT, REAL or TIME output value.
Note: The function converts strictly in accordance with IEC rules. Since this function has been realized as a generic function, there will also be a few illogical conversions, e.g. DINT_TO_BOOL.
When converting the data type DINT to the BOOL, BYTE, WORD, INT or UINT data type, the least significant bits of the input value are transferred to the output.
Negative input values cannot be converted into data types UDINT or UINT.

attribute.name: TypeDescriptiveForm
attribute.value:
This function transfers the unchanged input value (IN) to the output if the input value is not less than the minimum value (MN) and does not exceed the maximum value (MX). If the input value (IN) is less than the minimum value (MN), the minimum value will be transferred to the output. If the input value (IN) exceeds the maximum value (MX), the maximum value will be transferred to the output.
The data types of all IN values and output values must be identical.
Formula OUT = IN, if (IN >= MN) & (IN <= MX) OUT = MN, if (IN < MN) OUT = MX, if (IN > MX)

attribute.name: TypeDescriptiveForm
attribute.value:
The function converts an input value of the REAL data type to a BOOL, BYTE, WORD , DWORD, INT, DINT, UINT, UDINT data type or into the TIME data type.
Note: The function converts strictly in accordance with IEC rules. Since this function has been realized as a generic function, there will also be a few illogical conversions, e.g. REAL_TO_BOOL.
When converting to BOOL, BYTE, WORD, INT or UINT, the least significant bits of the input value are transferred to the output.
When converting to INT, DINT, UINT, UDINT and TIME, the IEC 559 rules for rounding are applied.
The following example shows how the IEC 559 rounding is applied. 1.4 => 1 1.5 => 2 2.4 => 2 2.5 => 2 2.6 => 3
Negative input values can not be converted into data types UINT, UDINT or TIME.

attribute.name: TypeDescriptiveForm
attribute.value:
This function block is used for counting INT values upward. A "1" signal at the R input causes the value "0" to be assigned to the CV output. With each transition from "0" to "1" at the CU input, the value of CV is incremented by 1. When CV is >= PV, the Q output is set to "1".
Note: The counter only works to the maximum values of the data type being used. No overflow occurs.
This function block specification is defined in IEC 61131-3 and only works with the INT data type.

attribute.name: TypeDescriptiveForm
attribute.value:
The function block produces a PID controller. A system deviation ERR is formed because of the reference variable SP and the controlled variable PV. This deviation ERR causes the manipulated variable Y to change.
The function block has the following properties: - real PID controller with independent gain, ti, td setting - Operating modes: Manual, Halt, Automatic - bumpless changeover between manual and automatic - Manipulated variable limiting in automatic mode - Separately enabled P, I and D component - Anti-windup reset - Anti-windup measures taken only for an active I component - definable delay of the D-component - D component connectable to controlled variable PV or system deviation ERR
Transfer function: 1 td * s G(s) = gain * (1 + ------ + --------------) ti * s 1 + td_lag * s - ------ ---------- P I D | | +------ YD (only when en_d = 1) | +------------------ YI (only when en_i = 1) +------------------------- YP (only when en_p = 1)
